bug_semantics: CodeIgniter 4 file-upload rules is_image and mime_in classify an upload solely by content-derived MIME type and never independently enforce that a non-empty client filename extension is a safe image/matching type. is_image maps UploadedFile::getExtension() (MIME-guessed, not the client name) through Mimes::guessTypeFromExtension() and accepts the file if that type starts with 'image'. mime_in compares UploadedFile::getMimeType()/getType() (finfo of the temp file) against the allowed list. An attacker can prepend image magic bytes (for example GIF89a) to a PHP webshell named shell.php; both rules pass, and if the application then saves the upload with the client-supplied name into a web-accessible script-enabled directory, the file is executed as PHP (CWE-434). The attack requires all three of: is_image/mime_in used without a separate safe-extension check (ext_in on patched versions), preservation of the original filename, and a public executable upload path.
flaw_origin: The missing client-extension check was present in the first public write of both rules. On 2016-09-18 Lonnie Ezell committed 2bd4f8f5053d97715d5ad320e08cac7ef20da104 ('New File validation rules.'), adding is_image (system/Validation/FileRules.php:93-111) as guessTypeFromExtension($file->getExtension()) with a leading-'image' test, and mime_in (lines 125-139) as in_array($file->getType(), $params). At that same revision UploadedFile::getExtension() already returned Mimes::guessExtensionFromType($this->getType()) and getType() used finfo_file/mime_content_type on the temp path; getClientExtension() existed but was documented as untrusted and was not used. The same commit's user guide described is_image as MIME-based and mime_in as a mime-type check. Later copies (StrictRules FileRules, 2021) and the 2024 move of the implementation into system/Validation/StrictRules/FileRules.php preserved that mechanism. The 2026-05-20 ext_in advisory GHSA-2gr4-ppc7-7mhx/CVE-2026-48062 patched only ext_in; is_image and mime_in remained content-only until 4.7.4.

HEAD UploadedFile::getExtension() still prefers guessExtension() (MIME-derived) over getClientExtension().

Fix b6e9a4fa1dca2df3d3f261bdf61532df8c6420aa (2026-06-30, Michal Sniatala, single parent 20ebcf4694d96d3c97fbc3938e360730e4f54618, GitHub 'Merge commit from fork', no public inner member). Adds hasInvalidImageClientExtension() to is_image (reject non-empty client ext whose guessed type is not image/*) and hasMismatchedClientExtension() to mime_in (reject when getClientExtension() != guessExtension()). Tests in FileRulesTest.php use GIF payload + name shell.php. reasoning: Vulnerability-first: GHSA-mmj4-63m4-r6h5 / CVE-2026-63223 is a real CWE-434 upload-validation gap, confirmed on CVE.org and not withdrawn. The exploitable sink is is_image/mime_in accepting a dangerous client extension when content looks like an allowed image/MIME. The smallest public first-write of those rule bodies is Lonnie Ezell's 2016 commit 2bd4f8f5053d97715d5ad320e08cac7ef20da104; its parent f3d286b9e6ac38d39cdd1ef5c59742e34fe3a1b3 lacks both functions, and no later commit introduced the missing-check (they only copied, moved, or renamed MIME APIs). The 2024 StrictRules relocation and 2021 StrictRules copy are therefore not BICs. The May 2026 ext_in security merge is a related incomplete remediation of a sibling rule, not the introducer of this mechanism. The June 2026 single-parent fork merge b6e9a4fa1dca2df3d3f261bdf61532df8c6420aa is the direct fix and lands in v4.7.4, matching the advisory. AI judgment is BIC-only: the 2016 commit object has human author/committer identity and no AI trailers, so the verdict is NOT_AI.
